annotations.category_path: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program / Total Benefitsa* / Budget Authority
annotations.variable_note: Section 501 of division HH of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023, requires states to replace benefits that were stolen during fiscal years 2023 and 2024. CBO’s cost estimate for that legislation included the cost to replace benefits in those years only. In its February 2024 baseline, CBO changed the treatment of that provision and included the cost of replacing those benefits in its spending projections for all years after 2024. That change was made to be consistent with section 257 of the Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act of 1985, which requires CBO to assume that most large expiring programs will continue to operate as they would immediately before their scheduled expiration. In the June 2024 baseline, CBO estimates that the cost of benefit replacement will be about 0.1 percent of benefits issued in each year, on average, totaling about $1.5 billion over the 2024-2034 period.
